label: main clause after when clause
explanation: It fires on tokens in the main clause following a comma that closes a temporal or conditional subordinate clause, especially a “When … ,” clause, and not on the preceding clause or ordinary text. It fires most strongly on the early predicate/verb phrase of a short declarative result, and weakly on longer, question, or non-When comma clauses.
